memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Also at your times of rejoicing—your appointed festivals and New Moon feasts—you are to sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, and they will be a memorial for you before your God. I am the Lord your God." - Num 10:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The trumpets were not only for battle and trouble. They were also sounded in times of rejoicing — at festivals and feasts, over the offerings of worship. The same instruments that called God's people in the day of danger also rang out in the day of gladness. God gave His people a way to celebrate before Him.

This is a lovely reminder that our God is a God of joy as well as help. We often turn to Him in our troubles, and rightly so. But He also invites us to celebrate in His presence, to sound the "trumpets" of praise and thanksgiving in the good times. Worship is not only for sorrow; it is for joy.

Notice, too, that these joyful blasts were "a memorial for you before your God." Our worship and rejoicing rise before God like a remembrance. He delights when His people are glad in Him. Joy offered to God is itself a form of worship.

Sometimes we forget to bring our joys to God — to thank Him, celebrate with Him, and rejoice in His goodness. We treat Him as an emergency contact for hard times only. But He wants to share our gladness too.

The New Testament calls us to "rejoice in the Lord always" (Phil 4:4). Every good gift comes from His hand (Jas 1:17), and every joy is a reason to lift our praise. Sound the trumpets of joy today. Bring your gladness to God, and celebrate His goodness before Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you bring your joys to God, or only your troubles?
- How can you "sound the trumpet" of praise and thanksgiving today?
- What good gift from God can you celebrate right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You share in my joys as well as my troubles. Help me to sound the trumpet of praise, celebrating Your goodness before You today. Amen.
